items.title: JLab Authorization Manager User Guide
items.text:
The JLab Authorization Manager (JAM) records the Director of Operations' authorization to run each of Jefferson Lab's facilities: which RF segments may run high power RF, and which beam destinations may take beam, in which beam mode and up to what current. It also tracks the credited controls that must be in place for each segment and destination, and the verification of each control by its responsible team. An operation is approved only while the director's permission and all of its controls' verifications are current; JAM revokes permission when either expires, or when a team downgrades a control, and tells the people concerned by email and logbook.

At JLab, JAM is at ace.jlab.org/jam. You can view it without logging in; log in to make changes.

The guide's website has a copy for each release; pick the version the Help tab shows. On GitHub, this guide describes the main branch, which may be newer than the version you are using.

items.title: Contents
items.text:
1. Concepts: facilities, RF segments and beam destinations, credited controls and verification teams, the director's permission, approval, expiration and roles.
  2. Authorizations: reading a facility's authorization, and giving or changing permission. For operators and authorizers.
  3. Verifications: checking control status, and verifying or downgrading controls. For verification teams.
  4. Expirations and notifications: when permission and verifications expire, and the emails and log entries JAM sends.
  5. Inventory: the controls, facilities, segments, destinations, participation, authorizers, watchers and verification teams.
  6. Administration: the Setup tab, settings and the administrator's tasks. For administrators.

items.title: Tabs at a glance
items.text: Tab What it is for Authorizations Each facility's current authorization for RF and beam operations, and its history. Authorizers change it here. Verifications The verification status of each credited control, segment and destination. Verification teams verify controls here. Inventory The credited controls and where they apply, the facilities, segments and destinations, and who authorizes, watches and verifies. Setup Administrators only: settings and the directory cache. Help Version, contacts, documentation and a feedback form.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
Operators: open Authorizations and pick the facility. Operate a segment or destination only if its Auth column shows a green thumbs-up, within the beam mode and current limit shown, until the expiration shown. See Reading an authorization.

Authorizers: on your facility's page, select Edit Beam Operations or Edit RF Operations, set each row, write the change notes, and Save. See Changing an authorization.

Verification teams: on Verifications, open a control with its arrow (→), select the rows you checked, choose Edit Verification, and set the status, dates and who verified it. See Verifying a control.

items.title: Questions and changes
items.text:
Use the feedback form on the Help tab, or contact the content and technical contacts listed there. To suggest a change to this guide, open an issue or pull request on GitHub.

JAM follows the Accelerator Safety Envelopes (ASE) and the Safety Assessment Document (SAD), which define the credited controls; at JLab see the CEBAF-LERF ASE, UITF ASE and SAD. Where this guide and those documents differ, the documents rule.

items.title: Administration
items.text:
User Guide › Administration

This page is for JAM administrators: users with the jam-admin role, who see the Setup tab. Administrators can also do what every other role can, for every facility and team: change any authorization and verify any control. What they do is still recorded under their own username. See Roles.

items.title: Setup tab
items.text: Page For Settings The app's settings; see Settings. Select a row to edit its value. Directory Cache JAM caches users' names, emails and roles from the user directory (Keycloak), and clears the cache every night at midnight. Clear it, or look up a user or role, after a change in the directory, such as a new verification team member. Users must log out and in again for a change to their own roles to apply.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Setup › Settings lists the settings with their descriptions.

Setting Use USER_QUERY_URL Where the username fields, such as Verified By, look up users. COMPONENT_QUERY_URL Where Edit Components searches for components (SRM). COMPONENT_DETAIL_URL The link from a component's name to its details (SRM); the name is added to the end. EMAIL_ENABLED, EMAIL_DOMAIN_NAME Email settings shared with JLab's other apps, such as for the Help tab's feedback form. JAM's own emails don't use them: they are always sent, to the username followed by @jlab.org or to the user's email in the directory. EMAIL_TESTING_ENABLED Send the administrators' and teams' emails to the users with the testlead role instead, and not to the facility manager. Watchers' emails are sent as usual. EMAIL_SENDER_ADDRESS The address JAM's emails are sent from. NOTIFICATION_* A banner shown at the top of every page, with an optional link. HELP_* The contacts and documentation links on the Help tab. ADMIN_ROLE_NAME Leave it jam-admin: JAM's own pages and checks use that role name. IP_READ_*, SMOOTHNESS_* Which addresses may view pages without logging in, and where shared web resources come from.

items.title: Regular tasks
items.text:
• Credited controls and participation: add or change controls on Inventory › Controls, and say where they apply on Inventory › Participation. Adding a control to a segment or destination makes it Not Verified at once, so plan it with its team and the authorizer.
  • Authorizers and watchers: keep Inventory › Authorizers and Inventory › Watchers current as people change jobs.
  • Verification team members: add or remove users from the team's role in the user directory, then clear the directory cache.
  • Components: list the components a verification covers; see Components.

items.title: Running the expiration check now
items.text: The expiration check for all facilities runs every night at midnight. To run it now, for example after correcting an expiration date, open /jam/ajax/expiration (at JLab, ace.jlab.org/jam/ajax/expiration) while logged in as an administrator. It answers {"stat":"ok"} when done. It also sends the upcoming expiration notices again.

items.title: What is changed in the database
items.text:
JAM has no pages to change these; a developer with database access changes them:

  • Facilities: name, URL path and order. The manager and logbooks are changed on Inventory › Facilities.
  • RF segments and beam destinations: name, facility, current units (beam), whether active, and order. An inactive segment or destination is hidden everywhere and is no longer checked for expiration; its history is kept.
  • Verification teams: name and directory role.

The beam modes of each facility are set in the code.

items.title: When notifications go missing
items.text: Log entries and emails are made in the background after each change, using a screenshot service and the logbook server. If an authorization changed but its Log Entry link never appears, or the emails have no picture, tell the technical contact on the Help tab: the change itself is saved.

items.title: Authorizations
items.text:
User Guide › Authorizations

The Authorizations tab shows each facility's current authorization. Pick the facility in the Auth list on the left. Anyone can read it; authorizers and administrators change it.

items.title: Reading an authorization
items.text:
A facility's page has an RF Operations panel, with a row per RF segment, and a Beam Operations panel, with a row per beam destination. A facility without segments or destinations has no panel for them.

Column Shows RF Segment or Beam Destination Its name. Select it to see the verification of each of its credited controls. Auth Whether the operation is approved: a green thumbs-up only when the director's permission allows it and its controls are Verified or Provisionally Verified, otherwise a red X. High Power RF (RF) The director's permission: Yes or No. Beam Mode (beam) The director's permission: a beam mode, or None. Current Limit (beam) The highest current allowed, in the destination's units, or Dump Power Limited when the director set no limit. Comment The authorizer's comment on this permission. It is outlined in gold when the permission relies on a Provisionally Verified control; the comment says why that is acceptable. Expiration When the permission ends, with (Expiring Soon) in red within seven days. Credited Controls Status The worst status of the operation's credited controls, with (Expiring Soon) when the earliest verification ends within seven days. Select the icon for each control's status and expiration.

Below each table:

  • Change Notes: the authorizer's notes on the latest change, or, after an automatic reduction, which segments or destinations JAM revoked.
  • Digital Signature: who authorized it and when. After an automatic reduction it adds "† Automatically reduced on" with the date; the signature stays the last authorizer's.
  • Log Entry: the logbook entry JAM posted for the latest change.
  • History: every earlier authorization; see History.

Opening a facility's page also runs that facility's expiration check, so a permission or verification that has just expired is revoked before the page shows it. See Expirations and notifications.

items.title: Changing an authorization
items.text:
You can change a facility's RF or beam authorization if you are one of its authorizers for that type (Inventory › Authorizers) or an administrator. Log in, and the panel shows Edit RF Operations or Edit Beam Operations.

  1. Select Edit RF Operations or Edit Beam Operations. Every row becomes editable.
  2. For each row, set the permission:
  3. RF: High Power RF Yes or No.
  4. Beam: the Beam Mode, and the Current Limit. Leave the limit empty for Dump Power Limited.
  5. Choosing No or None clears and locks the row's other fields.
  6. For each row with permission, set the Expiration date and time, and a Comment if needed.
  7. In Change Notes, write what you changed and why. The box starts empty; your notes replace the previous ones.
  8. Select Save, or Cancel to discard your changes.

Saving records a new authorization of every row, signed by you, so leave the rows you aren't changing as they are. JAM checks each row with permission, and refuses the save, naming the segment or destination, when:

  • its credited controls aren't Verified or Provisionally Verified;
  • its controls are Provisionally Verified and it has no comment explaining why permission is given anyway;
  • it has no expiration date; or
  • its expiration is less than one hour from now.

items.title: After you save
items.text:
The page reloads with the new authorization. Then, in the background, JAM:

  • posts a log entry, titled "JAM: Facility RF Authorization Updated" or "JAM: Facility Beam Authorization Updated", with a picture of the new authorization, to the facility's logbooks, as you; the Log Entry link appears when it is posted;
  • emails the same picture to the facility's watchers for that type, and to the administrators and the facility's manager.

See Expirations and notifications.

items.title: Restoring permission after a reduction
items.text: JAM revokes permission by itself when it expires or a credited control is downgraded or expires, but never restores it. Once the controls are verified again, an authorizer edits the authorization and gives permission again, with a new expiration.

items.title: History
items.text:
History, at the top right of each panel, lists the facility's RF or beam authorizations, the newest first, ten per page: when each was modified and by whom, when it was authorized and by whom, and its change notes. A row whose Modified By differs from its Authorized By is an automatic reduction, modified by jam-admin.

Destination Details or Segment Details shows that authorization's rows. Rows that changed from the authorization before it are highlighted in yellow. This page is also the picture JAM attaches to its emails and log entries.

items.title: Concepts
items.text: User Guide › Concepts

items.title: Facilities and operations
items.text:
A facility is a machine or test area JAM authorizes, such as CEBAF, LERF, UITF, CMTF or VTA. Each facility has a page on the Authorizations tab, a manager who is emailed about it, and the logbooks JAM posts its changes to.

JAM authorizes two operations types in each facility, separately:

  • RF operations, by RF segment: a part of the facility that runs RF, such as CEBAF's Injector, North Linac and South Linac, or a whole test facility ("Entire Facility"). The permission is whether the segment may run high power RF.
  • Beam operations, by beam destination: a dump, hall or other place beam may be sent, such as Hall A or the Inline Dump. The permission is a beam mode and a current limit.

A facility without segments or destinations has no panel for that type; VTA and CMTF, for example, have RF segments but no beam destinations.

items.title: Beam modes
items.text:
The beam modes depend on the facility:

Facility Beam modes CEBAF None, Tune, CW LERF None, Ceramic Viewer, Viewer Limited, High Duty Cycle, BLM Checkout, CW UITF None, Viewer Limited, Tune, CW

None means no beam. Each destination has its own current units, normally µA (uA). A destination with a beam mode but no current limit is Dump Power Limited: its current is limited only by the power its dump can take.

items.title: Credited controls
items.text:
A credited control is an engineered or administrative control that the safety envelope (ASE) credits for safe operation: shielding, Personnel Safety System (PSS) access and beam containment controls, oxygen deficiency hazard (ODH) controls, barriers and so on. Each control has a description, links to its documents, a verification frequency (how often it must be checked, or "As Needed"), and one responsible verification team.

A control participates in an operation when it is required for that RF segment or beam destination. Each pairing of a control with a segment or destination has its own verification: a status, when and by whom it was verified, when it expires, comments, an optional documentation link and, optionally, the components it covers.

items.title: Verification status
items.text:
Status Icon Meaning Verified Green thumbs-up The team has checked the control for this operation, until the expiration date. Provisionally Verified Yellow warning triangle The control is accepted with conditions. Permission is still possible, but the authorizer must explain it in a comment. Not Verified Red X The control isn't verified, or its verification expired or was downgraded.

A segment's or destination's status is the worst status of the controls that participate in it, and its expiration is the earliest of their expirations. A segment or destination with no participating controls counts as Verified. A facility's status for a control is likewise the worst of that control's verifications in the facility.

items.title: The director's permission
items.text: The Director of Operations, or a delegate (an authorizer), gives each facility's authorization: for each RF segment, high power RF Yes or No, and for each beam destination, a beam mode and current limit. Each permission other than None or No has an expiration date and may have a comment. Each save records a new authorization, with the change notes, who authorized it and when, so the history keeps every version.

items.title: Approved operations
items.text:
An RF segment or beam destination is approved, shown by a green thumbs-up in the Auth column of its facility's page, only while both:

  1. the director's permission allows it (high power RF is Yes, or the beam mode isn't None), and
  2. its credited controls are Verified or Provisionally Verified.

Operators must honor the permission as shown, and stay within its beam mode and current limit.

items.title: Expiration and automatic reduction
items.text:
Permissions and verifications expire. When a verification expires, JAM sets it to Not Verified, and when a team downgrades one, JAM keeps the team's new status; either way, JAM sets the permission of each segment or destination it affects to No or None. When a permission's own expiration date passes, JAM sets it to No or None too. These automatic reductions are saved as a new authorization, still signed by the last authorizer and marked "Automatically reduced", and are announced by email and log entry. JAM never raises a permission by itself: restoring it takes an authorizer.

Anything expiring within seven days is marked (Expiring Soon). See Expirations and notifications.

items.title: Roles
items.text:
Role Who Can Viewer Anyone, logged in or not See every page except Setup. Operator Operations staff Read and honor the authorizations. Operators need no special role. Authorizer Users listed as a facility's authorizers for RF or beam (Inventory › Authorizers) Change that facility's RF or beam authorization. Verification team member Users with the team's directory role (Inventory › Verifiers) Verify, or downgrade, the controls their team is responsible for. Gets the team's emails. Watcher Users listed as a facility's watchers for RF or beam (Inventory › Watchers) Gets an email each time that authorization changes. Facility manager The manager of a facility (Inventory › Facilities) Gets the facility's change and expiration emails. Administrator Users with the jam-admin role Do everything above for every facility and team, edit the inventory, and use the Setup tab.

Roles come from JLab's user directory (Keycloak); the authorizer, watcher and manager lists are kept in JAM.

items.title: Inventory
items.text:
User Guide › Inventory

The Inventory tab lists what JAM authorizes and verifies, and who is involved. Anyone can read it. Administrators can change the controls, facility managers and logbooks, participation, authorizers and watchers here; the rest is changed in the database (see Administration).

Page Lists Administrators can Controls The credited controls. Add, edit and remove controls. Facilities Each facility, its manager and its logbooks. Change a facility's manager and logbooks. Segments The active RF segments and their facilities. — Destinations The active beam destinations and their facilities. — Participation Which controls apply to which segments and destinations. Add or remove a control from a segment or destination. Authorizers Who may change each facility's RF or beam authorization. Add and remove authorizers. Watchers Who is emailed each facility's RF or beam authorization changes. Add and remove watchers. Verifiers The verification teams, their members and their controls. —

items.title: Controls
items.text:
Inventory › Controls lists each credited control's name, description, documents, verification team and verification frequency ("As Needed" when it has none). Select a team to see its members.

To change the list, select a row and Edit or Remove, or select Add:

  • Name and Description.
  • Documentation: links to the control's documents, as label|url, separated by commas; for example ASE|https://example.org/ase,Checklist|https://example.org/checklist.
  • Team: the verification team responsible for it.
  • Frequency: how often it must be verified, such as "1 Year". Verifiers use it to set expiration dates; JAM doesn't enforce it.

Warning: removing a control removes all of its verifications and their history, for every facility.

A new control applies nowhere until it is added on the Participation page.

items.title: Facilities
items.text:
Inventory › Facilities lists each facility's name, manager and logbooks. The manager gets the facility's change and expiration emails, and each authorization change is logged in its logbooks.

To change them, administrators select a facility's row and Edit:

  • Manager: the manager's username. Required.
  • Logbooks: the logbook names, separated by commas, such as TLOG,ELOG. Leave it empty to make no log entries for the facility.

items.title: Participation
items.text:
Inventory › Participation shows, for the facility you choose, a grid of credited controls against RF segments (RF Operations) and against beam destinations (Beam Operations). A ✔ means the control participates: it must be verified for that segment or destination.

Administrators select a cell to add or remove the ✔:

  • Adding a control creates its verification as Not Verified. The segment or destination becomes Not Verified, and so not approved, at once, until the team verifies the control. The director's permission stays as it was, so tell the authorizer and the team first.
  • Removing a control deletes that verification and its history.

items.title: Authorizers
items.text:
Inventory › Authorizers lists who may change each facility's RF or beam authorization; filter by facility, operations type or username. An administrator can change any authorization, listed or not.

Administrators select Add and choose the facility, the operations type (RF or BEAM) and the user, or select a row and Remove.

items.title: Watchers
items.text: Inventory › Watchers lists who is emailed each change to a facility's RF or beam authorization, including automatic reductions. Watchers need no role: anyone who wants to follow a facility, such as operations staff, can be one. Ask an administrator to add or remove you; they do it as for authorizers.

items.title: Verifiers
items.text: Inventory › Verifiers lists each verification team, its members, and the credited controls it is responsible for. Administrators also see the team's directory role. A team's members are the users with that role in JLab's user directory, so membership is changed there, not in JAM. Members can verify the team's controls and get the team's emails.

items.title: Expirations and notifications
items.text:
User Guide › Expirations and notifications

Every permission the director gives, and every Verified or Provisionally Verified control, has an expiration date. JAM checks for expirations, revokes what has expired, and warns people a week ahead.

items.title: When JAM checks
items.text:
• Every night at midnight, for every facility: JAM revokes what has expired, then sends the upcoming expiration notices.
  • Whenever someone opens a facility's page on the Authorizations tab: JAM revokes what has expired in that facility, so the page never shows an expired permission as current.

Something that expires during the day is therefore revoked when the facility's page is next opened, or at midnight, whichever comes first.

items.title: What expiration does
items.text:
1. Each Verified or Provisionally Verified control whose expiration has passed becomes Not Verified, with the comment "Expired". Its history gets a row modified by jam-admin.
  2. In the facility's current authorization, JAM sets to high power RF No, or beam mode None:
  3. each permission whose expiration has passed, with the comment "Permission automatically revoked due to director's authorization expiration"; and
  4. each permission of a segment or destination with a control that just expired, with the comment "Permission automatically revoked due to credited control control verification expiration".
  5. If any permission was revoked, JAM saves the result as a new authorization: its change notes list the segments or destinations revoked, it keeps the last authorizer's signature, and it is marked "Automatically reduced". Then JAM posts a log entry and sends emails, as below.

A downgrade by a verification team revokes permission in the same way, at once, with the comment "Permission automatically revoked due to credited control control verification downgrade".

If a control expires or is downgraded where there was no permission to revoke, only the verification changes: there is no new authorization, log entry or email.

items.title: Emails and log entries
items.text:
Each change to an authorization, whether by an authorizer or automatic, gets a log entry and emails with a picture of the new authorization. The log entry goes to the facility's logbooks (Inventory › Facilities), tagged Readme, titled "JAM: Facility RF Authorization Updated" or "JAM: Facility Beam Authorization Updated", and posted as the authorizer, or, for an automatic reduction, as the last authorizer. The email subjects start with "JAM: Facility".

Event Log entry Watchers Administrators and facility manager Verification team An authorizer saves an authorization Yes Yes Yes No A downgrade revokes permission Yes Yes Yes The downgraded control's team: "… Authorization Reduced due to Control Verification Downgrade" An expiration revokes permission Yes Yes Yes The team of each expired control: "… Authorization Reduced due to Control Verification Expiration" Upcoming expirations (nightly) No No Yes Yes, for the team's controls

Watchers get the RF or beam emails they are listed for (Inventory › Watchers). The administrators are the users with the jam-admin role, and the verification team is the users with the team's directory role.

Log entries and emails are made in the background after the change, and a failure doesn't undo the change. Always check JAM for the current authorization, as each log entry says.

items.title: Upcoming expiration notices
items.text:
Each night JAM emails "JAM: Facility Upcoming Expiration Notice" about what will expire between six and seven days later, so each expiration is normally announced once, a week ahead:

  • to the administrators and the facility's manager: the facility's RF and beam permissions and control verifications that will expire;
  • to each verification team: its control verifications that will expire.

The Expiring link on the Verifications tab lists everything expiring within the next seven days, and the Authorizations and Verifications pages mark it (Expiring Soon).

To keep an operation running, verify its controls again, or give a new permission, before it expires.

items.title: Verifications
items.text:
User Guide › Verifications

Each credited control must be verified, by its team, for each RF segment and beam destination it participates in. The Verifications tab shows where things stand, and is where teams record their checks.

items.title: The Verifications tab
items.text:
The tab has three panels, each of which can be collapsed:

  • Credited Controls: each control, with a section per facility listing its RF segments and beam destinations with their status icons. The arrow (→) opens the control's page for that facility.
  • RF Segments: each segment, with its facility, its status and its earliest control expiration. The arrow opens the segment's page.
  • Beam Destinations: the same for each destination.

Filter narrows the tab to one facility, one verification team, or both. Expiring, at the top right, lists every verification that expires within seven days, by facility.

The icons are those of the verification status: a green thumbs-up for Verified, a yellow triangle for Provisionally Verified, a red X for Not Verified.

items.title: A control's page
items.text:
A control's page (Control Verification) lists the control's verifications in two panels, RF Operations and Beam Operations, one row per segment or destination. Filter picks the control (listed as team / control) and, optionally, one facility. Info shows the control's description, documents, team and verification frequency.

Column Shows Facility / RF Segment or Facility / Beam Destination Where the control applies. Verified The status icon, the verification date and who verified it. Expiration Date When the verification ends. Components The components the verification covers, each with its status in SRM and a link to it there. Comments The verifier's comments, and a Documentation link if one was given. Audit History: every change to this verification.

Work on one control at a time from here: it lists exactly the rows your team is responsible for.

items.title: A segment's or destination's page
items.text: A segment's or destination's page lists the verification of each control that participates in it, as team / control, with the same columns. Its title shows its overall status and earliest expiration. Choose another segment or destination from the list at the top. The same view opens in a dialog when you select a segment or destination on the Authorizations tab.

items.title: Verifying a control
items.text:
You can edit a verification if you have the directory role of the control's verification team (Inventory › Verifiers), or are an administrator. Log in first.

  1. Open the control's page (or a segment's or destination's page).
  2. Select the rows you checked. Hold down Ctrl or Shift (⌘ on a Mac) to select several, or use Select › All. Rows of several segments or destinations can be edited together, as long as they are your team's.
  3. Select Edit Verification. The dialog lists the rows you selected, and notes when their current values differ.
  4. Fill in:
  5. Status: Verified or Not Verified.
  6. Verification Date: when it was checked; Now fills in the current time.
  7. Verified By: who checked it; Me fills in your username.
  8. Expiration Date: when it must be checked again, normally from the control's verification frequency. Required for Verified, and it can't be in the past. Not Verified clears it.
  9. Comments, and a Documentation URL, such as a checklist or work record.
  10. Select Save. The same values are saved to every selected row.

Every save is kept in the row's History. The dialog doesn't offer Provisionally Verified.

items.title: Downgrading a control
items.text:
Saving a lower status than a row had, such as Not Verified for a Verified row, is a downgrade. A downgrade revokes the director's permission at once: JAM sets each affected segment to high power RF No, and each affected destination to beam mode None, with a comment naming the control. It saves that as a new authorization, posts a log entry, and emails the facility's watchers, the administrators and manager, and the control's team. See Expirations and notifications.

Downgrade a control as soon as it can no longer be relied on; don't wait for its expiration.

Verifying a control again doesn't restore permission: the facility's authorizer must authorize it again.

items.title: Components
items.text:
A verification can list the components it covers, such as the PSS devices of a segment. The components come from SRM, and their status icons show SRM's status: a component that isn't Ready in SRM may need the control checked again. The components are for information; they don't change the verification's status.

Administrators add or remove components: select one row, then Edit Components, search for a component by name and Add it, or pick one and Remove it.

items.title: Verification history
items.text: History in a row's Audit column lists every change to that verification, the newest first, ten per page: when it was modified and by whom, the verification date, who verified it, the status, comments and expiration. When a verification expires, JAM adds a row modified by jam-admin, with Not Verified and the comment "Expired".
